top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Alberto Contador's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.
97ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Alberto Contador. Practice on paved Mediterranean mountain roads through the: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 86 miles.
8,327ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At mile 60 of 86, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
At Gran Fondo Alberto Contador, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Alberto Contador. Train it until it feels boring.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Alberto Contador. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
8,327ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved Mediterranean mountain roads through the can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 8,327ft of climbing on paved Mediterranean mountain roads through the does to your power file on race day.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 86 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Alberto Contador’s 86 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Gran Fondo Alberto Contador. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Gran Fondo Alberto Contador rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on paved mediterranean mountain roads through the costa blanca interior to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, TT Threshold, and Road Specific to prepare you for 86 miles of paved mediterranean mountain roads through the costa blanca interior in Oliva, Valencia, Spain.
